Research and Context

Project goal: by adapting the tour to the segmented audience, we aim to increase revenue

Foundation: split the tour into two segments: learners and players. For the former, provide the full version of the tour with all educational screens. For the latter, show a shorter version of the tour, excluding all questions about development, tips, etc.

Research results

— previous approach to audience segmentation in the tour

— the previous experiment involved determining the distribution of the main segments:

  • Start learning guitar from scratch
  • Play my favorite songs

Other experiments:

[2024-04-23] UG App: tour branch for those learning guitar from scratch — team brainstorming on personalizing the tour for those who are just starting to learn guitar

— the first experiment is about goal-setting in the tour. Based on it and its results, we will gather the current version

Hypothesis

If we segment the audience in the tour and show a shortened version to those who don't want to learn, we will increase conversion by 10%, because we will show each audience only the questions relevant to them.

Description of the Solution & Mockups

Iteration 1

Iteration 1

Solution

A

  • Add a screen with a segmentation question about learners and players to all variations, including the control version
    • apart from this new screen, the control version remains unchanged
    • the control version does not change regardless of the chosen answer on the first segmentation screen

B

  • In the test version, depending on the answer on the first screen, we create two branches
    • B for players
      • When selecting "Play my favorite songs" or "Something else" direct the user to the branch with the shortened tour, removing all questions about development, skills, and singing
    • B for players
      • If the answer "Start learning from scratch" is selected, direct the user to the full tour, similar to the current one

        • In this branch, remove the screen with the level question (assuming all are beginners)

        • On the instrument selection screen, change the heading to “Which instrument do you want to play?”

Iteration 2

Iteration 2

Solution

Based on the previous iteration where we saw a 4.5% decrease in the iOS conversion rate, with no positive impact on other metrics like tour success rate and retention rate, we can conclude that there are screens among those removed that were actually boosting conversions. So, in the next iterations, we want to figure out which specific screens are increasing conversions and which ones don't affect them at all.

  • B - In the test version, depending on the answer on the first screen, we create two branches
    • B for learners - no changes
      • If the answer "Start learning from scratch" is selected, direct the user to the full tour
    • B for players
      • When selecting ‘Play my favorite songs’ or ‘Something else,’ direct the user to the branch with the shortened tour, removing screens with the following questions:
        • How would you prefer to sing your favorite song? + "sounds good" hook screen after
        • How often do you sing? + "our users improve singing skills" hook screen after

Iteration 3

Solution

In the last iteration, we didn't see any changes in the "playing" path after we dropped four "sing" screens. So, this time we'll try the same changes for the "learning" path and update the "playing" path by removing some more screens.

  • B - In the test version, depending on the answer on the first screen, we create two branches
    • B for learners - no changes
      • When selecting "Start learning from scratch" direct the user to the branch with the shortened tour, removing screens with the following questions:
        • How would you prefer to sing your favorite song? + "sounds good" hook screen after
        • How often do you sing? + "our users improve singing skills" hook screen after
    • B for players
      • When selecting ‘Play my favorite songs’ or ‘Something else,’ direct the user to the branch with the shortened tour, removing screens with the following questions:
        • What's your preferred learning style?
        • Do you have a favorite song that you like to sing to your friends?

  • At the same time, we made the tour shorter, which slightly increased the passability in test variations
  • In addition, a shorter tour is less tiring for the user, which will affect their experience with the app (reducing negative reviews in stores)
  • We consider the experiment successful, we are rolling out a test variation

Next steps

  • Continue worsening ab-tests (taking into account the updated branding)
